newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 14.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 137 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media commented on Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's accusation that Democratic Party members were spreading gloom about Hong Kong overseas.

-- MING PAO said Tung should consider why the Democratic Party had been forced to go to the West for support. It said Tung had excluded members of the Democratic Party, the most popular party in Hong Kong, from his new government, and still had not promised that present Urban and Regional councillors could stay on in their posts after the handover. If Tung did not want Democratic Party members to voice their opinions overseas, he should include them in the establishment, the paper said.

-- APPLE DAILY said some people had claimed Tung wanted to copy the authoritarian style of veteran Singapore leader Lee Kwan Yew. But the paper said Lee had a strong character and foresight and refused to be controlled by other people. The editorial also asked why Tung was so afraid of criticism.

-- The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said Tung's comments were good for Hong Kong's prosperity and stability and helped guarantee Hong Kong people's freedom of speech. While Hong Kong needed freedom of speech, this kind of freedom must not be distorted into letting people say anything they like, depart from facts, mislead international society, confuse public opinion and harm Hong Kong's interests, the paper said.
